## Data analysis

For inferential statistics, Bayesian models were constructed using the Stan probabilistic programming language [@stanpaper] and fitted using the `cmdstanr` interface [@cmdstanr] in R [@R]. The choice of a Bayesian modeling framework allow us to naturally handle missing data in a wide class of models. This was important as it enabled us to model data from the project as *intention-to-treat* with the uncertainty associated with missing values incorporated into the posterior estimates.

A general workflow was adopted where models were incrementally built and tested for validity through simulations [@gelman2026]. First, implications of prior distributions were evaluated using prior-predictive simulations. Priors were selected to constrain model predictions and parameter values to *a priori* plausible ranges. This approach encourages the use of weakly informative priors on model parameters, which regularize models and shrink estimates and predictions without distorting the influence of the data on inference [@lemoine2019;@mcelreath2020;@gelman2014]. In relevant cases, synthetic data were used to confirm that model inferences were not biased by model misspecification. Samples from the joint posterior distribution were used to create posterior predictive checks, in which model implications are simulated and compared with characteristics of the observed data [@gelman2014, p. 141]. Selected models were also assessed for inferential capabilities using synthetic data simulations where parameter values are known. The sensitivity of model specifications to inference was assessed by comparing predictions across different models.

All sampling from prior and posterior distributions were done using the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) no-U-turn sampler ([Stan Reference Manual: MCMC sampling](https://mc-stan.org/docs/reference-manual/mcmc.html)). Performance of the HMC algorithm was assessed through chain convergence statistics (R-hat) and visually inspecting converging and stationary sampling across multiple HMC chains.

Descriptive data are presented as mean and standard deviation (SD). Inferential statistics are presented as full posterior densities, and percentile intervals (PI), or probability statements derived from full posterior distributions. 
 

## Description of the data set and participants

The overall objective of the present analysis is to determine the effect of krill oil supplementation in combination with resistance training on glucose metabolism and indicators of metabolic health. Outcome variables in the analysis are:

- Whole blood fatty acid composition, including omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids and the omega-3 index
- Blood glucose in response to a oral glucose tolerance-test
- Metabolic syndrome (derived from sub-scores)
   * Triglycerides
   * Waist circumference
   * Blood pressure 
   * HDL Cholesterol
   * Fasting glucose
- Body mass index
- Relative fat mass
- HOMA2-IR
- Adiponectin
- LDL Cholesterol
- HbA1c


```{r}

# Source figure options, packages, and main data prep.
source("./R/fig-opt-fun.R")
source("./R/packages.R")
source("./R/data-prep.R")
source("./R/helpers.R")

# Settings
refit.models <- FALSE

```



```{r}
#| label: data-prep-participants


part <- AOData::idkeys  
  
## Descriptives data 
baseline_dat <- AOData::bodycomp |>
  select(participant, time, lean.whole, BMC.whole, fat.whole)  |>
  mutate(weight = lean.whole + BMC.whole + fat.whole) |>
  inner_join(part) |>
  filter(time == "T1") |>
  ## Calculate height based on weight (DXA) and BMI 
  mutate(height = 100 * sqrt((weight/1000) / bmi)) |>
  ## Calculate relative lean and fat
  mutate(lean.rel = 100 * (lean.whole / weight), 
         fat.rel = 100 * (fat.whole/weight), 
         # Weight in kg
         weight = weight / 1000) |>
  select(participant, 
         treat, 
         completed, 
         sex, 
         age, 
         height, 
         weight, 
         bmi) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = age:bmi)
  
  
## Included participants 
total_participants <- baseline_dat |> 
  distinct(participant) |> 
  pull(participant)




# Per completed period
# dat |> 
#   summarise(.by = c(completed, treat, sex, name), 
#             m = mean(value), 
#             s = sd(value), 
#             min = min(value), 
#             max = max(value))
  
# Total

# Calculate n
n_total <- baseline_dat |> 
  filter(name == "age") |> 
  summarise(.by = c(treat, sex), 
            n = n()) 

n_groups_sex <- n_total |> 
  with(setNames(n,paste0(treat,sex)))

N <- sum(n_total$n)
```

At enrollment, participants were randomized into two groups, an active treatment-group (krill-oil fatty acids, 1 mg day^-1^) and a placebo control group (Placebo; @fig-figure1, @tbl-participants).

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Flow of participants through the trial, presented according to the CONSORT 2025 statement. All randomized participants were included in the analysis of outcomes, with missing follow-up data imputed."
#| label: fig-figure1
#| fig-width: !expr 180/25.4
#| fig-height: !expr 140/25.4


figure_01 <- readRDS("figures/figure-01.RDS")

figure_01


```



```{r}
#| label: tbl-participants
#| tbl-cap: "Participant characteristics."


baseline_dat |> 
  summarise(.by = c(treat, sex, name), 
            m = mean(value), 
            s = sd(value), 
            min = min(value), 
            max = max(value), 
            n = n()) |> 
  mutate(stats = paste0(
    sprintf("%.1f", round(m, 1)), 
    " (", 
    sprintf("%.1f", round(s, 1)), 
    ") [",
    sprintf("%.1f", round(min, 1)), 
    " - ", 
    sprintf("%.1f", round(max, 1)), 
    "]"), 
    n = n) |> 
  
  dplyr::select(treat, sex, name,n, stats) |> 
  

  
  dplyr::select(-n) |> 
  
  pivot_wider(names_from = treat, 
              values_from = stats) |> 
  
  mutate(sex = if_else(sex == "m", "Male", "Female"), 
         name = case_when(
           name == "age" ~ "Age (years)", 
           name == "height" ~ "Stature (cm)", 
           name == "weight" ~ "Body mass (kg)", 
           name == "bmi" ~ "Body mass index (kg&times;m^-2^)", 
           TRUE ~ NA )) |> 

  group_by(sex) |> 
  gt() |> 
  fmt_markdown() |> 
  
  cols_label(omega = md(paste0("Krill oil<br>(&male; n = ", 
                               n_groups_sex["omegam"], 
                               "; &female; n = ", 
                               n_groups_sex["omegaf"], ")")),
             ctrl = md(paste0("Placebo<br>(&male; n = ", 
                              n_groups_sex["ctrlm"], 
                              "; &female; n = ",
                              n_groups_sex["ctrlf"], ")")), 
             sex = "", 
             name = "") |> 
  tab_footnote(footnote = "Data are presnted as Mean (SD) [Min-Max]")

```

Participants were given krill oil or placebo in a supplementation-only period followed by a lead-in and combined period (supplementation and resistance training; @fig-figure2)
